vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw360
Version: 0.1.8

The openclaw360 skill is a runtime security tool for AI agents designed for prompt injection detection, tool authorization, and skill scanning. It follows security best practices by using pinned Git commits for installation (commit 5fd69db), disabling automatic model invocation, and restricting its file system operations to a dedicated configuration directory (~/.openclaw360/). The instructions provided in SKILL.md are consistent with its stated purpose and include explicit requirements for user confirmation before installation or initialization, with no evidence of malicious intent or data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill's claimed purpose (local runtime security, scanning other skills, local backups) aligns with its instructions and required files; it is instruction-only and asks the user to install a pinned GitHub commit and create a local config/identity directory — review the pinned commit before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (prompt-injection detection, tool authorization, DLP, skill scanning, backup/restore) match the declared requirements: python3 and local config paths under ~/.openclaw360. No unrelated cloud credentials or privileged system access are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions restrict operations to local analysis of user-provided text and SKILL.md/script files in user-specified skill directories and to the ~/.openclaw360/ directory for its own data. One minor inconsistency: the SKILL.md references a default scan path of ~/.openclaw/skills/ (missing '360'), which looks like a typo and could change which directories are scanned; otherwise the instruction scope stays within the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec in the registry (instruction-only), but SKILL.md includes pip install commands that fetch a pinned commit from GitHub. Using a pinned commit is good practice, but pip installing from a remote repo executes upstream code — the user should review the pinned commit before running the install commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables and only local config paths under ~/.openclaw360 (config, identity keys, audit, backups). Those paths are proportional to a local security/audit/backup tool. No unrelated credentials or system-wide config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and disable-model-invocation is set to true, so it will not be invoked autonomously by the model. It does create local identity keys and backups in its own directory, which is consistent with its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent for a local runtime-security tool, but because it requires you to run pip install against a GitHub commit and will create local signing keys and backups, you should: (1) manually review the pinned commit (5fd69db) on the GitHub repo before installing, (2) run the install commands yourself in a controlled environment (consider a venv), (3) confirm you’re comfortable with the tool creating ~/.openclaw360/ and an Ed25519 keypair for local signing, and (4) note the SKILL.md's default scan path typo (~/.openclaw/skills/) and ensure the scanner will target only directories you expect. The skill claims no network activity after install and no access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or other sensitive directories — verify these behaviors by inspecting the repo if you need higher assurance.
